inputs.share_count_basis: 47,529,953,984 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim report note 14); the company states it had no potentially dilutive ordinary shares in H1 2026 or H1 2025, so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: there is no SBC and no planned issuance.
inputs.cash_composition_note: RMB 161,700m cash and cash equivalents + RMB 152,678m time deposits with maturity over three months but within one year + RMB 11,892m current other financial assets (bank wealth-management products), all at 30 June 2026. Time deposits and the financial assets are included because they are short-dated bank instruments a resource company holds as a cash reserve, and the interest they earn is stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule). total_debt is loans and borrowings only (RMB 1,447m current + RMB 56,125m non-current); lease liabilities of RMB 10,516m are EXCLUDED because leases are charged inside the flows (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: none: CNOOC Limited operates no share-based payment scheme. No SBC line appears in the FY2018-FY2025 consolidated cash flow statements and EquityAwardTaxes is 0 every year; this is a verified zero, not a gap.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases nil (RMB 661m in FY2024, RMB 623m in FY2022). The flat share count is a fact of the register, not a modelling convention that needs funding.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at CNY/HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T06:58Z). Parity check: the FY2025 final dividend was declared at HK$0.55/share and booked at RMB 22,722m = RMB 0.478/share, implying 1.150 HKD/CNY at the March 2026 declaration date, within 2% of today's rate; the A-share (600938.SS) quotes in CNY and is not a clean parity because of the persistent A/H premium.
inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC 9.0%, identical across scenarios (risk is charged once, in the scenario flows). Cost of equity ~9.5%: CNOOC's revenue is Brent/Dubai-benchmarked and effectively USD-linked, so the risk-free anchor is the USD 10-year (~4.0%) rather than the 1.8% CNY CGB yield that financial repression holds down; beta 1.1 x ERP 5.0%. Debt is ~8% of capital at ~2.7% after tax. Blended 8.95%, rounded to 9.0%. No ad-hoc SOE/sanctions premium is stacked on top; those risks live in the bear scenario and its 25% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease payment (FY2025 principal RMB 3,381m + interest on lease liabilities RMB 492m = RMB 3,873m, 0.97% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path = 1.0% every year; lease liabilities (RMB 10,516m) excluded from net debt. Chosen because CNOOC's leases are FPSOs, vessels and rigs that recur with production, so an ongoing charge is more faithful than a one-off liability. Reported D&A already excludes right-of-use depreciation in the component build to the extent the lease charge replaces it.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests of RMB 2,505m (30 June 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is RMB 51-66m/yr, immaterial.
inputs.dismantlement_treatment: Provision for dismantlement (RMB 118,734m at 30 June 2026, already discounted) deducted in the equity bridge as a debt-like claim. Actual abandonment spend is tiny today (RMB 573m utilised in FY2025, RMB 2,478m in FY2024) and is NOT inside capex, so the forward flows carry almost none of this obligation; deducting the book provision charges it exactly once. This is the single largest conservative judgment in the bridge, worth about RMB 2.5 (HK$2.9) per share.
inputs.dividend_bridge_note: Two dividends that a buyer at the 2026-10-09 price never receives are deducted from the 30 June 2026 cash: the FY2025 final dividend (RMB 22,722m, declared H1 2026, sitting in other payables at balance date, paid July 2026) and the 2026 interim dividend of HK$0.94/share (declared 26 Aug 2026, record date 11 Sep 2026, so the price is ex; HK$44,678m / 1.1721 = RMB 38,118m). FCF accrued since 30 June is, by the folder's convention, not added back.
inputs.mid_cycle_note: FY2025 (realized oil US$66.47/bbl, Brent average US$68.2) is treated as the mid-cycle anchor year, not H1 2026 (realized US$85.49, a geopolitical spike). FY2025 owner FCF on the component build (EBITDA 249,364 - lease 3,873 - D&A 79,771 = EBIT 165,720; 28% cash tax; + D&A - capex 111,555) is RMB 87.5bn, which ties to the cash-flow-statement owner FCF of RMB 88.6bn (97,487 - 5,062 interest - 3,873 lease). Base case lets FY2026 run +12% on the known H1 strength with H2 moderating, then reverts -6% in FY2027 to a ~US$70 mid-cycle deck with ~3% volume growth, and grows at volume (2-3%) thereafter. Peak H1 2026 earnings are not extrapolated.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row: operating company, non-US and cyclical), with the adaptations file applied: currency-matched WACC, one lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for time deposits vs stripped interest income, SBC-zero market (house and street coincide, band_position null), and risk charged once (same WACC all scenarios, cyclicality in the flows). CNOOC is a pure upstream oil and gas producer: ~777 mmboe/yr net production, all-in cost US$27.9/boe, 69% of volume from China offshore, 31% overseas (Guyana Stabroek 25%, Brazil Buzios/Mero). Cash taxes paid FY2025 RMB 45.7bn on PBT RMB 169.6bn = 27%, so 28% is used; the special oil gain levy sits above EBITDA in opex and is why bull-case margin expansion is restrained. Working capital capture 0%: receivables + inventory (RMB 50.7bn) are below trade payables (RMB 72.3bn) and oil-price-driven swings are noise. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF for a cyclical (the house default is 20x), which binds in base and bull at WACC 9% / g 2-2.5%.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle volume growth: FY2026 production target 780-800 mmboe vs 777.3 actual (+1.6% midpoint) and a 2-3% multi-year volume runway from Guyana/Brazil and Bohai; the trailing CAGRs are not usable as a forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.2% vs revenue 20.7% and EPS 35.6%: every 5-year CAGR is measured from the FY2020 COVID oil trough (Brent US$42) and every 3-year CAGR from the FY2022 peak (Brent US$99), so they describe one oil cycle, not a trend. Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on reported FCF less interest income less lease principal and interest (FY2020 RMB 7.9bn, FY2022 RMB 118.4bn, FY2025 RMB 88.6bn).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-9.2%) is below reported FCF (-7.8%) because interest income on the growing cash pile (RMB 3.0bn -> 5.1bn) and lease payments (RMB 2.8bn -> 3.9bn) both rose while FCF fell; SBC is zero throughout so it plays no part.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +12%: H1 2026 revenue was +16.9% YoY on US$85 realized oil and +3.7% volume; H2 assumed to moderate toward US$75. FY2027 -6%: oil reverts to a ~US$70 mid-cycle deck (FY2025 realized US$66 at Brent US$68) while volume grows ~3%. Thereafter volume-only growth of 2-3% fading to 2%, flat real price.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 62.6%, FY2024 61.7%, FY2021 62.3%, FY2019 60.8%, FY2018 57.5%; H1 2026 63.9% at peak price. Mid-cycle 60-61%, easing to 60% as new deepwater barrels carry higher unit cost (all-in cost rose to US$29.7/boe in H1 2026).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided RMB 112-122bn (cash basis ~RMB 112bn = 25% of elevated revenue); FY2023-FY2025 cash capex ran 28-29% of revenue. Capex is set by plan, so the % rises when revenue reverts. D&A 20-21% (FY2025 20.0%, FY2024 17.7%) leaves net reinvestment of ~6% of revenue, consistent with a depleting asset growing volume 2-3%.

bull.narrative: Oil holds US$80-85 structurally on geopolitical supply loss and under-investment; Guyana (8 Stabroek projects by 2030) and Brazil (11 Buzios units by 2027) deliver 3.5-4% volume growth; unit costs stay near US$28/boe. Margin gain is restrained to ~2pp because the special oil gain levy claws back part of every dollar above US$65.

bear.narrative: H2 2026 oil slides as the spike unwinds; FY2027 Brent settles at US$55-58 (OPEC+ volume war plus a China demand slowdown), taking revenue down 22% and the EBITDA margin to 54% because D&A and the capex plan are sticky in RMB. Volume growth slows to 1-2% as non-operated Guyana/Brazil pacing is outside CNOOC's control. Energy-transition demand erosion and a tighter US sanctions regime (1260H/CMIC) cap the terminal multiple at 10x and terminal growth at 1%.

scenario_narratives.base: CNOOC is a low-cost (US$28-30/boe all-in), net-cash, volume-growing offshore producer whose earnings are a near-linear function of Brent. The base case anchors on FY2025 as the mid-cycle year (realized US$66, Brent US$68): FY2026 benefits from the known H1 price spike and 780-800 mmboe production, FY2027 reverts to a ~US$70 deck, and value thereafter comes from 2-3% volume growth out of Bohai, Guyana and Brazil at a ~60% EBITDA margin and 27-28% capex intensity. Terminal value is bound by the 12x cyclical cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structurally higher oil (US$80-85) plus faster deepwater delivery and stable unit costs. Requires two independent things to go right: price and non-operated project pacing.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027 price-down cycle to the high US$50s with sticky capex and D&A compresses owner FCF by ~45% in the trough year; growth is volume-only and slower; sanctions and transition risk hold the exit multiple at 10x. The balance sheet (RMB 269bn net cash before dividends) keeps the dividend intact, so this is an earnings bear, not a solvency bear.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear is raised to 25% because a pure-play commodity producer sits one oil-price regime change from the bear path (FY2020 proved it) and the sanctions/governance axis is a standing structural risk outside management's control. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs both a sustained above-mid-cycle oil deck and non-operated partners (ExxonMobil in Guyana, Petrobras in Brazil) to deliver on schedule. With spot oil currently above mid-cycle the near-term skew is to bull, but the ten-year distribution around a mid-cycle anchor is roughly symmetric, hence equal tails.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the mid-cycle owner FCF of a depleting, reinvesting asset base at a currency-consistent 9% WACC with a cyclical 12x terminal cap; treat the RMB 326bn cash pile as surplus (its interest stripped from the flows), but deduct the two dividends already committed out of it, the minority stake, and the dismantlement provision that forward capex does not carry. The result is intentionally below what a peak-earnings or sell-side EV/EBITDA framing would give.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oil price: every US$10/bbl on ~600 mmbbl of liquids is ~RMB 43bn of revenue, roughly 45% of base-year owner FCF, before the special oil gain levy offset.
Mid-cycle anchor could be wrong in either direction: if US$70 Brent is too high for a decarbonising demand curve the base case overstates; if under-investment keeps US$80+, the bull case is the base.
Dismantlement deduction (RMB 118.7bn, HK$2.9/share) is a judgment: a reader who treats abandonment as fully absorbed by perpetual reinvestment would add it back.
Time deposits and wealth-management products (RMB 164.6bn) are counted as cash; if a portion is restricted (dismantlement fund accounts) or trapped by capital controls, net cash is overstated.

Terminal cap 12x binds in base and bull; CNOOC has historically traded 3-5x EV/EBITDA under the SOE/sanctions discount, so realizing the model value requires either a re-rating or distribution of the cash flows (the 45% payout floor delivers the latter).
Sanctions escalation (OFAC CMIC, DoD 1260H) can impair H-share liquidity and the multiple independently of cash flows.
